topic: Orthogonal polynomial system in continuous and discrete settings

definition_paraphrases.paraphrase: On an interval (a,b), a sequence p_n of real polynomials with degree(p_n)=n is orthogonal relative to a nonnegative weight w if the weighted cross-integral ∫_a^b p_n(x)p_m(x)w(x) dx vanishes for every distinct n,m, subject to the DLMF stated positive finite zeroth moment and finite polynomial moments.

For an appropriate finite or countable subset X⊆R equipped with strictly positive point weights w_x, polynomials of consecutive degrees satisfy Σ_{x∈X}p_n(x)p_m(x)w_x=0 whenever n≠m, with the finite and infinite support cases and moment conditions specified separately.
A broader DLMF orthogonality notion replaces w(x)dx by an admissible Lebesgue–Stieltjes measure μ with finite moments of every order and requires ∫p_n(x)p_m(x)dμ(x)=0 for n≠m.

mathematical_comparison: Interval-density and point-mass weights are different realizations of orthogonality; both can be situated in a suitable measure-theoretic framework, but the exact source hypotheses about positive moments, admissibility and polynomial degree must be preserved. Do not flatten finite supported systems into an infinite degree-indexed sequence.

source_section: 4.10, The Reverse of Differentiation and Indefinite Integrals

definition_paraphrases.paraphrase: For real-valued f defined on an interval I, an antiderivative is a differentiable F on I satisfying F′(x)=f(x) at each x∈I where the derivative is defined.
If F is one antiderivative of f on an interval I, all others on I are exactly F+C for real constants C, because differentiable functions with equal derivatives differ by a constant on an interval.
The notation ∫f(x)dx denotes the general family F+C of antiderivatives, rather than a single uniquely determined real number or Riemann definite integral.

mathematical_comparison: On a disconnected domain, independent constants may be selected on distinct connected components. The standard single constant C statement requires the interval/connected-domain hypothesis and cannot be stated globally for arbitrary disconnected domains. An indefinite integral is related to, but not identical as an object to, a particular antiderivative.

topic: Finite limit of a real function at a real approach point

definition_paraphrases.paraphrase: Suppose f is defined at all x≠a sufficiently near a on both sides, and L∈R. Then lim_{x→a}f(x)=L means: for every ε>0 there exists δ>0 such that 0<|x−a|<δ implies |f(x)−L|<ε.

The same quantified inequality can be interpreted for x in a general subset D⊆R approaching a, provided a is an accumulation point of D; this source does not itself establish all general topological-domain formulations.

mathematical_comparison: The textbook's displayed definition assumes f is defined on an open punctured interval around a. General domain-relative limits require explicitly restricting the quantifier to x∈D and ensuring a accumulation; one-sided limits are separate directional contexts. No point value f(a) or continuity at a is required for the punctured limit.
